newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline tanker runs aground near mouth of NYH.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline tanker runs aground near mouth of NYH.

text.p: A 225-foot tanker carrying 631,000 gallons of gasoline ran aground Wednesday near the mouth of New York Harbor, but was refloated Thursday without leaking fuel or sustaining damage, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

"There was no hull damage and no damage to the environment," said Petty Officer Robert Lanier, noting the ship hit a sand bar Wednesday at 1930 EST/0030 GMT in East Rockaway Inlet, not far from Kennedy International Airport.
Lanier said the vessel, "Reliable II," was enroute to the Rad Oceanside Terminal in the East Rockaway Inlet to unload its cargo when it ran aground.
He was not immediately able to say where the ship was registered, or who owned it.
He noted Reliable II was refloated with the help of another tanker, "The Great Gull," which took on 126,000 gallons/3,000 barrels of Reliable II's cargo.
Once lightered, "Reliable II" was again floating above the sandbar that had snagged her hull by 0330 EST/0830 GMT.
"The Great Gull" had previously unloaded her own cargo at the same Rad Oceanside Terminal, Lanier said.
"Reliable II's" cargo of 631,000 gallons amounts to just over 15,000 barrels.
